story.soThat: I can quickly create similar bots or clean up unused ones

task.title: Create POST /api/v1/bots/{bot_id}/duplicate endpoint
task.details: Accept optional name parameter for new bot name. Validate user owns bot (RLS). Fetch source bot details. Create new bot with status "Empty", inheriting description and confidence_threshold from source. New bot gets unique bot_id and optional custom name or default "[source.name] (Copy)". Validate name uniqueness within tenant. Return new bot object. Audit log duplication with source_bot_id and new_bot_id.

task.title: Create DELETE /api/v1/bots/{bot_id} endpoint
task.details: Validate user owns bot (RLS). Check document count for bot. If >100 documents: enqueue background deletion job, return 202 Accepted with job_id. If ≤100 documents: execute synchronous deletion, return 204 No Content. Sync deletion: delete bot record (cascade handles foreign keys), delete documents from storage (S3/MinIO), delete embeddings from pgvector, delete chunks, delete chat history. Audit log deletion with timestamp and user.

task.title: Create BotDeletionService with async deletion task
task.details: Create tasks/bot_deletion.py with delete_bot_async(bot_id, tenant_id) method. Implement batch processing for large datasets: documents → storage → embeddings → chunks → chat history → bot record. Add error handling and retry logic (max 3 retries). Add progress tracking in Redis or database table. Create Celery task that calls BotDeletionService with proper error logging and alerting. Ensure Celery/Redis queue configured properly.

task.category: Backend - Deletion Progress API (Optional for MVP)

task.details: Return status (pending/in-progress/completed/failed), progress percentage, estimated time remaining. Use Redis or database table to track deletion jobs. Implement polling or SSE for real-time progress updates (optional for MVP; simple polling acceptable).

task.title: Add/verify CASCADE constraints in database schema
task.details: Ensure cascading DELETE constraints exist: documents.bot_id → ON DELETE CASCADE, chunks.document_id → ON DELETE CASCADE, embeddings.chunk_id → ON DELETE CASCADE, chat_sessions.bot_id → ON DELETE CASCADE. Create Alembic migration if constraints missing. Test cascade behavior in development: delete bot, verify all dependent records deleted automatically.

User can edit the new bot name before confirming

When user confirms duplication: New bot created with status "Empty", New bot inherits description and confidence_threshold, New bot does NOT inherit documents/embeddings/chat history, New bot gets unique bot_id

User redirected to new bot's page or bot list updates with new bot
Original bot remains unchanged

artifact.title: Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: Background Job Infrastructure: Celery + Redis queue for async tasks. Async deletion for bots >100 documents: enqueue task, return 202 Accepted, track progress in Redis/database. Retry logic: max 3 retries with exponential backoff. Error logging and alerting for failed tasks.

artifact.title: Technical Specification
artifact.snippet: Cascade Deletion: Use PostgreSQL CASCADE constraints for data integrity. Foreign key: documents.bot_id → ON DELETE CASCADE, chunks.document_id → ON DELETE CASCADE, embeddings.chunk_id → ON DELETE CASCADE, chat_sessions.bot_id → ON DELETE CASCADE. Background job handles object storage cleanup (S3/MinIO files).

artifact.title: Architecture Document
artifact.snippet: Mandate: Row-Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL + tenant_id context propagation in APIs. Use PostgreSQL + pgvector for MVP and early scale. All deletion operations must respect RLS policies and tenant isolation.

artifact.title: Epic Breakdown
artifact.snippet: Epic 2 covers Bot & Knowledge Management FR7-FR19. Story 2.2 enables users to duplicate bots (copy settings, not documents) for quick similar bot creation and delete bots (with cascade cleanup and background jobs for large datasets) for knowledge base cleanup. Includes RLS enforcement and async deletion threshold (100 docs).

artifact.snippet: FR10: Users can delete bots and associated documents with confirmation. FR11: Users can duplicate bots (settings only, no documents). FR12: Bots are isolated per tenant; deletion/duplication respects multi-tenancy. Large bot deletion (>100 docs) runs async with progress indication.

constraint.title: RLS Enforcement for Duplication and Deletion
constraint.details: Both duplicate and delete endpoints must enforce RLS to ensure users can only duplicate/delete their own tenant's bots. Validate tenant_id matches current user's tenant before operation. Return 403 Forbidden if attempting cross-tenant access. Pattern: tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')::uuid in all queries.

constraint.title: Async Deletion Threshold
constraint.details: 100 documents chosen as threshold for async vs sync deletion. If bot has ≤100 documents: synchronous deletion, return 204. If bot has >100 documents: async deletion, return 202 Accepted with job_id. Threshold configurable via environment variable BOT_DELETION_ASYNC_THRESHOLD. Rationale: small bots = instant feedback; large bots = prevent timeout, allow user to continue.

constraint.title: Duplication Scope
constraint.details: Duplication must copy ONLY: name (with "(Copy)" suffix or custom), description, confidence_threshold, tenant_id. Must NOT copy: documents, embeddings, chunks, chat_history, bot_id. Rationale: knowledge base and history specific to original context; user likely wants fresh KB for new use case.

constraint.title: Name Uniqueness for Duplicates
constraint.details: Duplicated bot names must be unique within tenant. If default name "[Original] (Copy)" already exists, generate "[Original] (Copy) 1", "[Original] (Copy) 2", etc., or reject with 409 Conflict if user provides duplicate name. Enforce (tenant_id, name) unique constraint at database level.

constraint.title: Cascade Deletion Integrity
constraint.details: Use PostgreSQL CASCADE constraints for referential integrity. When bot deleted: documents cascade-delete, chunks cascade-delete (via documents), embeddings cascade-delete (via chunks), chat_sessions cascade-delete. Background job handles object storage cleanup (S3/MinIO files) after cascading deletes complete. All cascades must complete successfully or entire deletion transaction rolled back.

constraint.title: Deletion Confirmation Security
constraint.details: Delete modal must require user to type exact bot name (case-sensitive) to confirm deletion. Delete button disabled until typed name matches exactly. No shortcuts or abbreviations accepted. This prevents accidental bulk deletions.

constraint.title: Optimistic Updates for UX
constraint.details: Frontend must remove bot from list immediately on delete submission (optimistic update), not wait for server confirmation. If deletion fails, restore bot to list and display error toast. Apply same pattern to duplication: add new bot to list optimistically, revert on error.

constraint.title: Background Job Error Handling
constraint.details: Celery tasks must implement retry logic: max 3 retries with exponential backoff. On final failure, log error, alert admin, and notify user via email or in-app notification with retry option. Do not silently fail. Track job status in Redis or database for user visibility.

constraint.title: API Response Codes
constraint.details: POST /duplicate: 200 (sync) or 202 (if future async option added). DELETE: 202 Accepted (async, large bot) or 204 No Content (sync, small bot). 404 Bot not found. 403 Forbidden (cross-tenant RLS). 409 Conflict (duplicate name in duplication). 400 Bad Request (validation errors). 401 Unauthorized (no JWT). 500+ Server errors.

standards.paragraph: Backend tests use pytest with FastAPI TestClient. Follow Story 2.1 patterns: mock JWT tokens with tenant_id in payload, use fixtures for authenticated clients and test database. All database tests verify RLS enforcement by confirming queries return only current-tenant data and forbidden access for other tenants. Test both sync (≤100 docs) and async (>100 docs) deletion paths separately. Verify cascade deletion: delete bot, confirm documents/chunks/embeddings/chat_history deleted automatically. Mock S3/MinIO file operations or skip in unit tests (integration tests can test real storage cleanup). Frontend tests use Vitest + React Testing Library with mocked API calls via MSW or simple fetch mocks. Mock useBotsQuery hook to control list state during modal tests. E2E tests use Playwright with full user flows: login, navigate, duplicate bot, verify new bot appears, delete bot with confirmation, verify removed. All tests isolated, deterministic, no external dependencies (mock all API calls).

idea.description: Test POST /bots/{bot_id}/duplicate: verify new bot created with status "Empty", unique id, inherits description and confidence_threshold from source, does NOT inherit documents/embeddings/chat_history. Verify source bot unchanged.

Test DuplicateBotModal rendering and interactions: default name "[Original] (Copy)" appears in input, user can edit name, form validates name length 2-50 chars, live uniqueness check (mock API call), submit button disabled until valid.

Test name uniqueness in duplication: create bot "HR Bot", duplicate to "HR Bot (Copy)" (succeeds), attempt to duplicate again to same name (409 Conflict). Test custom name conflict: duplicate with provided name "HR Bot" (409).
Test success toast: after successful duplication, verify toast displays "Bot duplicated: [New Bot Name]" and closes after 3-5 seconds.

Test DeleteBotModal confirmation: delete button disabled initially, user types bot name in input, button enabled only when typed name matches exactly (case-sensitive). Test "Bot Name" vs "bot name" vs "Bot name" all treated as different (case-sensitive).

Test cascade deletion: create bot with documents, chunks, embeddings, chat sessions. Delete bot. Verify bot record deleted, all documents deleted (including from storage), all chunks deleted, all embeddings deleted, all chat sessions deleted.
Test sync deletion (≤100 docs): delete small bot, verify 204 No Content response, bot removed from list immediately, success toast "Bot deleted: [Bot Name]".

Test async deletion (>100 docs): delete large bot, verify 202 Accepted response with job_id, progress toast "Deletion in progress. This may take a few minutes.", bot removed from list immediately, user can navigate away (deletion continues background), optional polling shows progress updates.
Test RLS enforcement: user from tenant A creates bot, user from tenant B attempts to duplicate/delete that bot, verify 403 Forbidden response, bot not modified.

Test error handling in modals: mock API error response (500), verify inline error message displays in modal, user can close modal or retry. Test network error (timeout), verify user-friendly error message.

Test E2E duplication flow: user logs in, navigates to bot list, clicks "Duplicate" on "HR Bot", edits name to "HR Bot v2", confirms, new bot "HR Bot v2" appears in list with same description and threshold as original. Test E2E deletion flow: user clicks "Delete" on "Sales Bot", types "Sales Bot" in confirmation input, confirms, "Sales Bot" removed from list and navigates to list view.

Test modal open/close from BotCard actions menu: click three-dot menu on bot card, verify "Duplicate" and "Delete" options appear, click "Duplicate" opens DuplicateBotModal, click close modal returns to list. Test "Delete" opens DeleteBotModal similarly.

Test DeleteBotModal displays: bot name (bold, prominent), warning message text, document count (e.g., "5 documents"), confirmation input placeholder "Type the bot name to confirm", red danger-style delete button initially disabled.
